questions.markdown:
A scientist is studying two genes, A and B, in a plant species. Gene A controls flower color (red or white), and gene B controls leaf shape (rounded or jagged). The dominant allele for gene A is represented as A (red), and the recessive allele as a (white). Similarly, the dominant allele for gene B is represented as B (rounded), and the recessive allele as b (jagged).

To study the inheritance patterns of these traits, the scientist performs a dihybrid test cross between a plant heterozygous for both traits $(AaBb)$ and a plant homozygous recessive for both traits $(aabb)$. The offspring display the following phenotypes and numbers:

- Red flowers, rounded leaves: 40
- Red flowers, jagged leaves: 10
- White flowers, rounded leaves: 12
- White flowers, jagged leaves: 38

i) Exhibit the cross in the form of a Punnett square.

ii) Identify the parental and recombinant phenotypes.

iii) Calculate the recombination frequency for these genes (factors).

iv) Based on your calculations, determine whether these genes are likely linked or assort independently.
